market_specific_notes: Dallas neuro-evaluation shoppers usually need a cleaner comparison of testing depth, report usefulness, and adult-versus-child fit instead of generic diagnosis language.
The best local comparison in Dallas is whether a clinic explains scope, turnaround, and what the written report is actually for.
local_vetting_points: Ask whether the evaluation is screening-only or a full diagnostic workup.
Ask whether the report is built for school, workplace, accommodations, treatment planning, or just confirmation.
Ask which age groups the clinician routinely evaluates.
Ask whether the evaluator explains ADHD vs autism vs broader neuropsych routing before testing.
Ask what local records or collateral input make the report stronger.
typical_cost_ranges: Pricing in Dallas often shifts based on testing depth, interview time, collateral review, and report complexity.
A low quote is not meaningful if it excludes report quality or follow-up explanation.
payment_options: Ask whether the clinic is private pay only, offers superbills, or helps with reimbursement paperwork.
Ask whether intake, testing, scoring, feedback, and report delivery are billed together or separately.
wait_time_notes: Wait time should be judged by intake delay, testing date, and final report delivery together.
A fast intake call does not guarantee fast testing or fast reporting.
availability_notes: Availability should include adult versus child slots, tele-intake options, and the realistic report turnaround after testing.
Ask whether cancellation openings are common if timing matters.
named_resources_or_providers: Dallas-area academic medical centers, psychology networks, and accommodations-oriented provider directories are more useful than generic testing-near-me lists.
Use local specialty fit and report purpose as part of the comparison.
Local academic medical centers, children’s hospitals, psychology clinics, and accommodations-oriented provider directories should be compared by report purpose, not only name recognition.
city_intro_override: Dallas neuro-evaluation shoppers should compare testing scope, report purpose, adult-versus-child fit, insurance/reimbursement path, and report turnaround before choosing a provider.

primary_city_decision_block.title: City-specific neuro evaluation decision checklist
items: Decide whether the question is ADHD, autism, learning, memory, concussion/TBI, or a broader differential evaluation.
Ask what the written report can support: school, work, therapy planning, medication discussion, or legal/medical documentation.
Compare intake-to-testing-to-report timeline, not only first appointment availability.
Ask whether the provider routinely works with the age group and evaluation purpose you need.
Ask whether pricing reflects screening only, full testing, collateral review, feedback, and written recommendations.
Confirm insurance, superbill, reimbursement, prior-authorization, and records requirements before scheduling.

testing_scope_notes: Ask whether the clinic offers screening, diagnostic clarification, ADHD-focused testing, autism-focused testing, or a broader differential workup.
Testing depth should match the real decision you need to make.
insurance_reimbursement_notes: Ask whether the clinic accepts insurance, provides superbills, or expects full private-pay reimbursement follow-through from the patient.
Do not assume testing is covered just because intake is covered.
adult_vs_child_fit: Confirm whether the clinician routinely evaluates adults, children, or both, and whether the testing approach changes by age group.
report_turnaround_notes: Ask when the written report is delivered, whether feedback is separate, and whether accommodations-ready language is included when relevant.
